## Purpose and entry points
Budibase is a TypeScript/Svelte monorepo for building, deploying, and operating data-backed apps, automations, and AI agents. The main HTTP runtime is the Koa server at `packages/server/src/index.ts`, assembled through `packages/server/src/app.ts` and API route registration in `packages/server/src/api/index.ts`. A separate worker runtime handles global/system administration APIs via `packages/worker/src/index.ts`.

## Browser applications
The Builder is the authoring SPA: `packages/builder/src/main.js` boots `packages/builder/src/App.svelte`; route files under `packages/builder/src/pages/builder/workspace/[workspaceId]` cover data, app design, automations, APIs, and agents. It persists edits through frontend API clients in `packages/frontend-core/src/api`.

The Client is the runtime renderer for end-user apps. `packages/client/src/index.ts` initializes `packages/client/src/components/ClientApp.svelte`, which interprets stored screen/component definitions and invokes app APIs. Both frontends are Svelte; reusable UI and grid/data facilities live in `packages/bbui/src/index.ts` and `packages/frontend-core/src/components/grid`.

## Server API and workspace domain
`packages/server/src/api/routes/index.ts` maps HTTP endpoints to controllers in `packages/server/src/api/controllers`. Controllers delegate to workspace-scoped SDK modules under `packages/server/src/sdk/workspace`, creating a boundary between transport concerns and business/data operations. Authentication, workspace selection, authorization, validation, and feature checks are enforced through `packages/server/src/middleware` plus shared facilities in `packages/backend-core/src/middleware` and `packages/backend-core/src/security`.

Primary flow: Builder/Client → Koa route → controller → workspace SDK → persistence, integration, files, or asynchronous processing. The repository also exposes a documented public API, specified at `packages/server/specs/openapi.yaml` and implemented under `packages/server/src/api/routes/public`.

## Data, tenancy, and integrations
CouchDB is the principal document-store foundation, abstracted in `packages/backend-core/src/db/couch/DatabaseImpl.ts`; tenant/workspace database separation is represented by `packages/backend-core/src/tenancy/tenancy.ts`. Server SDKs own internal/external table and row behavior, notably `packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/tables` and `packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/rows`.

External business data access is normalized through integration adapters in `packages/server/src/integrations`, including SQL, REST, S3, CouchDB, Redis, Google Sheets, and cloud databases. Object storage is abstracted by `packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/objectStore.ts`, allowing S3-compatible storage. Redis supports caching, locks, and queues through `packages/backend-core/src/redis`.

## Automations, agents, and asynchronous work
Automation definitions are shared between UI and backend in `packages/shared-core/src/automations`; execution and triggers are implemented in `packages/server/src/automations`, with concrete actions in `packages/server/src/automations/steps`. Automation workers are separately deployable, reflected by `charts/budibase/templates/automation-worker-service-deployment.yaml`.

AI agent lifecycle, prompts, tools, conversations, knowledge bases, and LLM execution are centered in `packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai`. Agent tools enforce authorization in `packages/server/src/ai/tools/authorization.ts`; chat/webhook adapters reside in `packages/server/src/api/controllers/webhook`. AI model routing can use LiteLLM, configured in `hosting/litellm_config.yaml`, while RAG queues and SharePoint knowledge synchronization are implemented in `packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai/rag`.

## Events and realtime boundaries
Domain changes publish through the shared event system in `packages/backend-core/src/events`; document updates can trigger downstream processors. Server WebSocket endpoints in `packages/server/src/websockets` push Builder, Client, and grid updates, separating request/response APIs from live synchronization. Redis-backed queues and locks are the main coordination boundary for multi-instance and background work.

## Deployment topology
Self-hosted deployment supports Docker Compose (`hosting/docker-compose.yaml`), a consolidated single-image runtime (`hosting/single/Dockerfile`), and Helm/Kubernetes (`charts/budibase/values.yaml`). Helm deploys distinct app-service, worker, automation-worker, proxy, Redis, CouchDB, MinIO, and LiteLLM services. Nginx proxy configuration lives in `hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf`; CouchDB, Redis, and MinIO provide persistence, cache/queue coordination, and object storage respectively. The CLI entry point `packages/cli/src/index.ts` manages hosting lifecycle and backups.
